BURSEVI:v1p250#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p250#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p250#2/r1.claim: The command to cease must cover disbelief as well as fighting: merely stopping combat does not entitle the former combatants to forgiveness, much less mercy.
BURSEVI:v1p250#2/r1.anchor: عن القتال وكذا عن الكفر فإن الانتهاء عن مجرد القتال لا يوجب استحقاق المغفرة فضلا عن استحقاق الرحمة

BURSEVI:v1p250#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p250#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p250#2/r2.claim: If they cease, God forgives their past deeds and is merciful to them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r1.claim: If ending the conflict means only ceasing combat, the verse is abrogated; under the two preceding interpretations it remains operative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r1.anchor: وعلى قول: إن الانتهاء عن القتال فقط، تكون الآية منسوخة، وعلى القولين قبله تكون محكمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r2.claim: Intahā means to desist; it is an iftaʿala form describing an action the subject performs upon himself, like iḍṭaraba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى: انتهى: كف، وهو افتعل من النهي، ومعناه فعل الفاعل بنفسه، وهو نحو قولهم: اضطرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r3.claim: The verse supports accepting repentance from deliberate murder: if disbelief is a greater sin than killing and God accepts repentance from disbelief, repentance from killing is accepted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245#2/r3.anchor: وفي قوله: فإن انتهوا فإن الله غفور رحيم دلالة على قبول توبة قاتل العمد، إذا كان الكفر أعظم مأثما من القتل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p271/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p271/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p271/r13.claim: The punishment of fighting, expulsion, and killing applies to unbelief, but God is forgiving and merciful to those who stop disbelieving and enter Islam, since Islam erases what came before.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p271/r13.anchor: ثم ذكر أن من كفر بالله فمثل هذا الجزاء جزاؤه من مقاتلته وإخراجه من وطنه وقتله، ثم أخبر تعالى أنه غفور رحيم

AKHFASH:v1p173/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p173/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p173/r1.claim: “If they desist, God is forgiving and merciful” means that God is forgiving toward them; the object “for them” is understood.
AKHFASH:v1p173/r1.anchor: أما قوله {فإن انتهوا فإن الله غفور رحيم} يريد: فإن الله لهم.

STUDYQURAN:2:190/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r5.claim: Some say the passage came after Ḥudaybiyah: Muslims had turned back from the ʿumrah in 628 under treaty terms, and as the next year's pilgrimage approached they feared attack and fighting in the sacred precinct during sacred months, so the verses set engagement guidelines.
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r5.anchor: Some report that these verses were revealed in connection

STUDYQURAN:2:190/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r16.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r16.claim: Some read “if they desist” to mean the idolaters stop idolatry and become Muslims.
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r16.anchor: Some also reason that if they desist means

STUDYQURAN:2:190/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r17.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r17.claim: Others say they need only desist from fighting and hostility.
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r17.anchor: though others simply state that it is the fighting and hostility from which they must desist

STUDYQURAN:2:190/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r18.claim: The conversion-as-final-goal interpretation is problematic in the verse's plain sense and in light of 9:6, which requires safe conduct for an idolater seeking asylum.
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r18.anchor: The interpretation that the conversion of the idolaters is the final goal is problematic

STUDYQURAN:2:190/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r19.claim: The author notes that this reading leaves little explained: hostilities begin for political reasons such as fighting and expulsion, yet supposedly end only through spiritual repentance and conversion.
STUDYQURAN:2:190/r19.anchor: little explanation is provided by the commentators who seem to take the position that hostilities begin with fighting and expulsion (political causes), but can end only with repentance and conversion to Islam (spiritual causes).

TAB-FULL:v3p299/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p299/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p299/r1.claim: If those fighting believers stop fighting and disbelief, repent, and return from past sins, God forgives them and grants them the hereafter's reward by His mercy.
TAB-FULL:v3p299/r1.anchor: رحيم به في آخرته بفضله عليه، وإعطائه ما يعطي أهل طاعته

TAB-FULL:v3p299/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p299/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p299/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses ‘if they desist’ as ‘if they repent.’
TAB-FULL:v3p299/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، فإن انتهوا فإن تابوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

TABATABAI:2:191-193/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:191-193/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:191-193/r7.claim: Here desisting means stopping fighting at the Sacred Mosque, not ending all fighting by accepting Islam; the latter is the sense of the second desistance clause in 2:193.
TABATABAI:2:191-193/r7.anchor: والمراد به الانتهاء عن مطلق القتال عند المسجد الحرام دون الانتهاء عن مطلق القتال بطاعة الدين وقبول الإسلام

TABATABAI:2:191-193/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:191-193/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:191-193/r8.claim: Each “if they desist” clause limits its nearest preceding statement, so the two clauses have different referents rather than repeating one another.
TABATABAI:2:191-193/r8.anchor: قيد لما يتصل به من الكلام من غير تكرار

TABATABAI:2:191-193/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:191-193/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:191-193/r9.claim: The statement that God is forgiving and merciful puts the cause in place of the effect, giving the reason for the ruling.
TABATABAI:2:191-193/r9.anchor: وضع السبب موضع المسبب إعطاء لعلة الحكم

TABATABAI:2:190-195#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:190-195#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:190-195#8/r1.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr transmits the preceding interpretation through several routes from Ibn ʿAbbās and others.
TABATABAI:2:190-195#8/r1.anchor: وروي هذا المعنى في الدر المنثور بطرق عن ابن عباس وغيره.

TABATABAI:2:190-195#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:190-195#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:190-195#8/r5.claim: The apparent unity of the passage indicates that these verses were revealed together.
TABATABAI:2:190-195#8/r5.anchor: وقد عرفت ان ظاهر وحدة السياق في الآيات الشريفة أنها نزلت دفعة واحدة.

TABRISI:2:192/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:192/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:192/r1.claim: Intihāʾ is abstaining; nahy is forbidding an act with a negative command and disapproval, while amr urges an act with a positive command and the commander's intent.
TABRISI:2:192/r1.anchor: الانتهاء الامتناع والنهي الزجر عن الفعل بصيغة لا تفعل مع كراهة الناهي لذلك الفعل والأمر الدعاء إلى الفعل

TABRISI:2:192/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:192/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:192/r2.claim: Al-nahy can also mean a pond that holds back water, and the plural nuhya means intellect; tanhiya is a hollow where rainwater ends or pools, and inhāʾ brings something to its limit.
TABRISI:2:192/r2.anchor: والنهي الغدير لمنعه الماء أن يفيض والنهي بمنزلة المنع ونهاية الشيء غايته

TABRISI:2:192/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:192/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:192/r3.claim: Maghfira is covering a sin so that, in legal judgment, it is treated as if it never occurred.
TABRISI:2:192/r3.anchor: والمغفرة تغطية الذنب بما يصير به بمنزلة غير الواقع في الحكم

TABRISI:2:192/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:192/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:2:192/r4.claim: Mujāhid and others explain desisting as repenting from unbelief.
TABRISI:2:192/r4.anchor: أي امتنعوا من كفرهم بالتوبة منه عن مجاهد وغيره

TABRISI:2:192/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:192/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:192/r5.claim: The conditional clause is abbreviated because the preceding context makes its omitted content clear.
TABRISI:2:192/r5.anchor: فاختصر الكلام لدلالة ما تقدم من الشرط عليه

TABRISI:2:192/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:192/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:192/r6.claim: The verse establishes that an intentional killer's repentance is accepted: God has declared that He accepts a polytheist's repentance, and association is graver than killing.
TABRISI:2:192/r6.anchor: وفيه الدلالة على أنه يقبل توبة القاتل عمدا لأنه بين عز اسمه أنه يقبل توبة المشرك

THALABI:v2p88/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p88/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p88/r6.claim: If they cease fighting and disbelief, God forgives what came before and is merciful to His servants.
THALABI:v2p88/r6.anchor: فإن انتهوا عن القتال والكفر فإن الله غفور لما سلف رحيم بعباده

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:191-193/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:191-193/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:191-193/r4.claim: Desisting means ceasing shirk, unbelief, and fighting and accepting Islam; God forgives their prior unbelief and fighting.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:191-193/r4.anchor: ثم بين أنهم إن انتهوا، أي: كفوا عن الشرك والكفر والقتال وأسلموا { فإن الله غفور رحيم } أي: يغفر لهم كفرهم وقتالهم من قبل،

ELMALILI:2:192-195/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:192-195/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:192-195/r1.claim: The command concerns Arab polytheists rather than People of the Book, as the wording about expelling them from where they expelled the Muslims indicates.
ELMALILI:2:192-195/r1.anchor: وَأَخْرِجُوهُم مِّنْ حَيْثُ أَخْرَجُوكُمْ kaydı delâletiyle bu âyetin ehl-i kitab hakkında olmayıp Arab müşriklerine mahsus olduğu anlaşılır.

ELMALILI:2:192-195/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:192-195/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:192-195/r2.claim: People of the Book could be accepted in submission through payment of the poll tax, while Arab polytheists were required to accept Islam or face the sword.
ELMALILI:2:192-195/r2.anchor: Ehl-i kitâbın vergi ile mutâva‘atı dahi makbul olabildiği hâlde Arab müşrikleri ya İslâm veya seyfe mahkumdur.

QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r9.claim: When intrusive thoughts and the soul’s enemies cease competing with God, quiet inner speech and its struggles; one charged with guarding secrets has no spare time for varied ego-combat.
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r9.anchor: إذا انقطعت عنك غاغة خواطرك وأعداء نفسك

QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r10.claim: The allusion concerns disciplining the self, one’s fiercest enemy, until human traces disappear and both self and heart surrender without planning or choice to God’s decree.
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r10.anchor: الإشارة من الآية إلى مجاهدات النفوس

QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r11.claim: Once the self surrenders, only the negligent remain liable; one who fulfills the command is released from its burden.
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r11.anchor: فإذا استسلمت النفس فلا عدوان إلا على أرباب التقصير

QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p92/r12.claim: When two claims both belong to God, submit to the ruling of the moment and its signs rather than prefer one for even a small personal interest, lest the heart be veiled from God.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:191/r40.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:191/r40.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:191/r40.claim: If the attackers desist, Muslims should cease fighting and not use violence against those who have stopped; God’s forgiveness and mercy are declared.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:191/r40.anchor: saldırıdan vazgeçilmesi halinde Allah’ın gafûr ve rahîm olduğu bildirilerek, müslümanların da, artık savaşmayı durduranlara karşı şiddet kullanmamaları gerektiği ima edilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:191/r41.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:191/r41.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:191/r41.claim: One report says that after the Hijra the Prophet first set out with many Muslims to visit Mecca, was blocked by the Quraysh at Hudaybiya, sought a peaceful settlement, and received permission to fight in these verses after a polytheist unit attempted an attack.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:191/r41.anchor: Hz. Peygamber, hicretten sonra ilk defa Mekke’yi ziyaret etmek üzere kalabalık bir müslüman grupla yola çıkmış; fakat Hudeybiye denilen yerde Mekkeli müşriklerin engellemesiyle karşılaşmış

FARRA:v1p115/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p115/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p115/r4.claim: If the opponents stop and have not initiated hostilities, there is no retaliation against those who desist; wrongdoing remains with those who started and persisted.
FARRA:v1p115/r4.anchor: فإن انتهوا فلم يبدءوكم فلا عدوان على الذين انتهوا، إنما العدوان على من ظلم: على من بدأكم ولم ينته.

SAMIN-DURR:2:192/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:192/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:192/r1.claim: The omitted complement of intahaw is عن القتال: if they desist, the condition means desist from fighting.
SAMIN-DURR:2:192/r1.anchor: ومتعلق الانتهاء محذوف؛ أي: عن القتال.

SAMIN-DURR:2:192/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:192/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:192/r2.claim: Intahaw is an iftaʿala form from nahā; its derivation from intahiyū involves deleting yāʾ after the heavy ḍamma, or changing yāʾ to alif after it moves and then deleting the alif at the meeting of two sukūns.
SAMIN-DURR:2:192/r2.anchor: وانتهى " افتعل " من النهي، وأصل انتهوا: انتهيوا، فاستثقلت الضمة على الياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r8.claim: He takes their stopping to mean abandoning unbelief and entering Islam, since forgiveness and mercy do not apply while they remain disbelievers; Qur’an 8:38 and the context support this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r8.anchor: فإن انتهوا فإن الله غفور رحيم أي: عن الكفر، ودخلوا في الإسلام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r9.claim: Another interpretation takes “if they desist” to mean desisting from both fighting and associating partners with God; he calls this a good interpretation because both precede it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r9.anchor: وقيل: فإن انتهوا عن المقاتلة والشرك، لتقدمهما في الكلام، وهو حسن،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r10.claim: A further view reads the condition as ending fighting alone; forgiveness then concerns God’s mercy to the Muslims in lifting the duty to fight, not forgiveness for the opponents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r10.anchor: وقيل: عن القتال دون الكفر، وليس الغفران لهم على هذا القول، بل المعنى:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r11.claim: The excerpt begins to report another view that the conditional has an omitted apodosis, but ends before giving its proposed wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p245/r11.anchor: حيث أسقط عنكم تكليف قتالهم، وقيل: الجواب محذوف، أي:

ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r1.claim: Mujahid and others explain “if they desist” as abandoning disbelief through repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r1.anchor: عن الكفر بالتوبة منه كما روى عن مجاهد وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r2.claim: Another view takes their desisting to mean stopping both disbelief and fighting, as the surrounding mention of both suggests.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r2.anchor: أو عنه وعن القتال كما قيل : لقرينة ذكر الأمرين

ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r3.claim: If they repent, God forgives their past wrongdoing.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r4.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r4.claim: Al-Bahr cites this verse to support acceptance of repentance by a deliberate murderer: disbelief is graver than murder, yet repentance from disbelief is accepted.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p76/r4.anchor: واستدل به في البحر على قبول توبة قاتل العمد إذ كان الكفر أعظم مأثما من القتل وقد أخبر سبحانه أنه يقبل التوبة منه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p214/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p214/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p214/r1.claim: If they stop fighting and disbelieving, God forgives what came before and is merciful to His servants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p214/r1.anchor: أي غفور لما سلف رحيم بالعباد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p362/r23.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p362/r23.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p362/r23.claim: Desisting means stopping both fighting and its preliminaries.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p362/r23.anchor: أي عن القتال ومقدماته , وفيه إشعار بأن طائفة منهم تنتهي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p362/r24.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p362/r24.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p362/r24.claim: God has always been Forgiving and Merciful, and this is how He treats anyone who repents.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p362/r24.anchor: أي له هاتان الصفتان أزلا وأبدا فكل من تاب فهذا شأنه معه

DURR-FULL:v1p495/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p495/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p495/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses their desisting as repentance.

IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r1.claim: Muqātil reads desisting as stopping their fighting and entering Islam.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r1.anchor: وبه عن مقاتل فان انتهوا عن قتالكم واسلموا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قوله : وان انتهوا فان تابوا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r3.claim: Muqātil says God forgives their former shirk when they accept Islam.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r3.anchor: وبالاسناد إلى مقاتل قوله فان الله غفور رحيم يغفر ما كان في شركهم اذا اسلموا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says God is merciful to them after repentance.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p327/r4.anchor: حدثني عطاء عن سعيد بن جبير قوله رحيم قال : رحيم بهم بعد التوبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r1.claim: If the opponents stop fighting, Muslims should stop killing them; believers should make forgiveness their practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { فإن انتهوا فإن الله غفور رحيم } أي فإن انتهوا عن قتالكم فلا تقتلوهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r2.claim: God's forgiveness and mercy do not logically follow from the enemy's cessation, so the clause elliptically implies “then forgive them”; this omission urges and supports the believers' forgiveness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r2.anchor: إذ كل سامع يعلم أن وصف الله بالمغفرة والرحمة لا يترتب على الانتهاء فيعلم أنه تنبيه لوجوب المغفرة لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r3.claim: Intahaw originally means to respond to a prohibition and then broadened to desist from an act or intention, since forbidding asks someone to leave an act whether begun or not.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r3.anchor: والانتهاء : أصله مطاوع نهى يقال : نهاه فانتهى ثم توسع فيه فأطلق على الكف عن عمل أو عن عزم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r4.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r4.claim: Al-Nabigha's line illustrates nahy used for forbidding the Banu Dhibyan from undertaking certain acts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p206#2/r4.anchor: قال النابغة : لقد نهيت بني ذبيان عن أقر وعن تربعهم في كل إصفار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p525#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p525#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p525#2/r1.claim: If the opponents stop fighting in the sanctuary and turn to Islam and repentance, God forgives their sins, even if they killed Muslims in His sanctuary; no sin is too great for Him to forgive when one repents.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p525#2/r1.anchor: أي: فإن تركوا القتال في الحرم، وأنابوا إلى الإسلام والتوبة

MUQATIL:2:190-193/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:190-193/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:190-193/r6.claim: If opponents stop fighting and affirm God’s oneness, He forgives their shirk and shows them mercy through Islam.
MUQATIL:2:190-193/r6.anchor: عن قتالكم ووحدوا ربهم، { فإن الله غفور } لشركهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p94#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p94#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p94#2/r1.claim: If they stop associating partners with God and fighting, God forgives their past transgression and mercifully accepts their repentance and faith.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p94#2/r1.anchor: عن الشرك والقتال ﴿ فإن الله غفور ﴾ لما سلف من طغيانهم ﴿ رحيم ﴾ بقبول توبتهم وإيمانهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:191-192#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:191-192#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:191-192#3/r6.claim: If they desist from fighting by embracing faith, God forgives their past sins and shows them mercy, as in 8:38.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:191-192#3/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فإن انتهوا } أي عن قتالكم بالإيمان فإن الله يغفر لهم جميع ما تقدم، ويرحم كلا منهم

RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r2.claim: Although fighting was commanded, this clause clarifies that its obligation ends when the opponents desist; repentance can remove an obligation even where some legal penalties persist.
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r2.anchor: بين بهذا أنهم متى انتهوا عن ذلك سقط وجوب القتل عنهم

RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads “if they desist” as stopping the fighting; the aim of permission to fight is to prevent the enemy from fighting.
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فإن انتهوا عن القتال وقال الحسن : فإن انتهوا عن الشرك

RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads “if they desist” as abandoning disbelief, since merely stopping combat would not earn an unbeliever God’s forgiveness and mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فإن انتهوا عن القتال وقال الحسن : فإن انتهوا عن الشرك

RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r5.claim: True cessation from disbelief requires both repentance and adherence to Islam; merely declaring the two testimonies publicly protects life, while reward and forgiveness require genuine faith.
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r5.anchor: الانتهاء عن الكفر لا يحصل في الحقيقة إلا بأمرين أحدهما : التوبة والآخر التمسك بالإسلام

RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r6.claim: The verse establishes acceptance of repentance from every sin and rejects the claim that repentance for intentional murder is never accepted: shirk is worse, and a repentant unbeliever may also be a killer.
RAZI-FULL:v5p112/r6.anchor: دلت الآية على أن التوبة من كل ذنب مقبولة ، وقول من قال : التوبة عن القتل العمد غير مقبولة خطأ
